_note: Layer 1 (settled law) for the basic structure feature. Every ruling and feature rests on the judgment itself: checked against the judges' own words (not headnotes or summaries) in November 2026, using the verbatim Supreme Court Reports text. Each item cites the report (S.C.R.) and the page or paragraph; 'at' holds those pinpoints per source.

struck_bs.what: Second part of Art. 31C (declaration clause), inserted by 25th Amendment
struck_bs.case: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala (1973)
struck_bs.ground: Khanna J said the second part “contains the seed of national disintegration”: letting a legislature shut out even limited judicial review strikes at the basic structure. Five other judges would have struck down all of Article 31C, saying it let legislatures wipe out basic rights and handed them the power to amend the Constitution

at.KB: pp. 759-760 (Khanna J) and the majority view, p. 1001

struck_bs.what: Art. 329A(4), inserted by 39th Amendment, which put the past elections of the Prime Minister and the Speaker beyond the election law and any challenge (Chandrachud J also held clause (5) void)
struck_bs.case: Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975)
struck_bs.ground: The majority judges gave different reasons: it destroyed free and fair elections, which are part of democracy (Khanna J); it settled an election dispute without applying any law, against democracy and the rule of law (Mathew J, Ray CJ); and it denied equality and took over the courts' work (Chandrachud J)

struck_bs.what: 42nd Amendment s.4 widening Art. 31C to ‘all or any of the principles laid down in Part IV’
struck_bs.case: Minerva Mills v Union of India (1980)
struck_bs.ground: Destroys the balance between Parts III and IV, an essential feature of the basic structure

struck_bs.what: Art. 368(4) and (5), inserted by 42nd Amendment s.55
struck_bs.case: Minerva Mills v Union of India (1980)
struck_bs.ground: A limited amending power is itself a basic feature. Clause (5) removed every limit on the power, and clause (4) shut out the courts

struck_bs.what: Art. 371D(5) and the condition attached to it (State Government could modify or annul tribunal orders)
struck_bs.case: P. Sambamurthy v State of Andhra Pradesh (1986)
struck_bs.ground: Violates the rule of law, ‘a basic and essential feature’; tribunal less effective than the High Court

struck_bs.what: Art. 323A(2)(d) and 323B(3)(d), to the extent they exclude Arts. 226/227 and 32
struck_bs.case: L. Chandra Kumar v Union of India (1997)
struck_bs.ground: Judicial review by High Courts and Supreme Court is part of the inviolable basic structure

struck_bs.case: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Assn v Union of India (2015)
struck_bs.ground: It breached the independence of the judiciary and the separation of powers, both part of the basic structure. The NJAC Act also fell, and the earlier system of appointing judges applies again

at.NJAC: para 244 (Khehar J), pp. 492-493, and Order of the Court, paras 2 and 4, pp. 1055-1056

struck_other.what: Para 7 of the Tenth Schedule (bar on courts)
struck_other.ground: Not ratified by half the States, as Art. 368(2) requires for such changes; rest of Tenth Schedule upheld

struck_other.what: Part IXB (co-operative societies), inserted by the 97th Amendment, except as it concerns multi-State co-operative societies
struck_other.case: Union of India v Rajendra N. Shah (2021)
struck_other.ground: Not ratified by half the States, as Art. 368(2) requires for such changes; the Part still applies to multi-State co-operative societies

at.KB: pp. 280-281 (Shelat and Grover JJ) and p. 322 (Hegde and Mukherjea JJ)

outside_or_upheld.what: Right to property is not part of the basic structure
24th Amendment, 25th Amendment s.2 (Art. 31(2)) and 29th Amendment upheld; Golak Nath overruled

Ninth Schedule laws added on or after 24 April 1973 get no blanket protection: tested against the basic structure as reflected in Art. 21 read with Arts. 14, 19 and their principles. Laws already upheld by the Court can't be reopened on these principles; actions and transactions already finalised stay protected

Ordinary laws cannot be struck down just for violating the basic structure. A law falls only if it breaks a provision of the Constitution, such as a fundamental right, or the legislature had no power to make it
103rd Amendment (EWS, Arts. 15(6), 16(6)) upheld 3:2. The lead majority opinion (Maheshwari J, joined by Trivedi J) said the 50% ceiling is not inflexible

at.JANHIT: Order of the Court; Maheshwari J, para 102

outside_or_upheld.what: Challenge to ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ in the Preamble (42nd Amendment) dismissed; the power to amend extends to the Preamble
Arts. 15(5) and 21A (93rd and 86th Amendments) do not alter the basic structure
Ending Art. 370's application upheld; Art. 370 was a temporary provision
Rest of the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection) upheld
